title: Orecchiette Dough
instructions:
Orecchiette Dough

Puglian orecchiette made with durum semolina, water, olive oil, and salt.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

2 1/3 cups finely milled durum semolina
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp plus 1 tsp warm water
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2/3 tsp fine salt
3 tbsp semolina for dusting

Preparation

1. Make a well in the semolina on a work surface.

2. Dissolve the salt in the warm water.

3. Gradually pour the water into the center.

4. Add the olive oil.

5. Gradually draw in the semolina.

6. Knead for at least 10 minutes, until smooth, firm, and elastic.

7. Cover with a towel or plastic wrap.

8. Rest for 20–30 minutes.

9. Divide the dough into several pieces.

10. Roll into ropes about the thickness of a finger.

11. Cut into pieces about 3/8 inch long.

12. Place the smooth edge of a knife over each piece.

13. Press and drag the dough toward you across the work surface.

14. Turn the disk over your thumb to create the characteristic cup shape.

15. Arrange on a semolina-dusted tray.

16. Dry for at least 30 minutes.

17. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

18. Cook for about 5 minutes, or until the orecchiette rise and are tender but still firm.

19. Drain.

Service

Dress immediately with the intended sauce.

Chef's note

Dragging with the knife creates the rough surface that helps orecchiette hold sauce.

title: Strascinati Dough

Strascinati Dough

Puglian semolina pasta shaped by dragging each piece under the fingers.

title: Fileja Dough

Fileja Dough

Calabrian semolina pasta rolled around a thin metal rod.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

3. Gradually add the water.

4. Knead vigorously for at least 10 minutes.

5. Continue until smooth and firm.

6. Cover with a kitchen towel.

7. Rest for 30 minutes.

8. Divide into several pieces.

9. Roll into ropes about the thickness of a pencil.

10. Cut into pieces 1 1/4–1 1/2 inches long.

Keep the rod diagonal to create fileja's characteristic elongated hollow shape.

Busiate Dough

Sicilian semolina pasta twisted around a thin rod.

10. Roll into thin ropes.

11. Cut into lengths about 3–4 inches.

12. Place a thin rod along each rope.

13. Wind the dough around the rod on a diagonal.

14. Roll lightly on the work surface to set the spiral.

15. Slide off gently.

16. Arrange on a semolina-dusted tray.

17. Dry for at least 30 minutes.

18. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

19. Cook for 5–6 minutes.

20. Drain.

Dress with pesto Trapanese, basil pesto, or another Sicilian sauce.

Do not wind the dough too tightly around the rod; it should slide off easily without losing the spiral.

Sicilian Maccarruna Dough

Fresh Sicilian semolina pasta with eggs and water, rolled around a thin rod.

Ingredients

2 large eggs
1/2 cup plus 2 tbsp warm water
2/3 tsp fine salt

1. Make a well in the semolina.

2. Crack the eggs into the center.

3. Add the salt.

5. Knead while gradually drawing in the semolina.

6. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons water only if needed to create a firm, elastic, nonsticky dough.

7. Knead for 10 minutes.

8. Shape into a disk.

9. Cover.

10. Rest for 20–30 minutes.

11. Roll the pasta about 1/16–1/8 inch thick.

12. Cut into small squares or short strips.

13. Place one piece over a thin knitting needle or pasta rod.

14. Press with your palm and roll so the dough wraps around the rod.

15. Slide off gently.

16. Arrange on a semolina-dusted tray.

17. Dry for 30–60 minutes.

18. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

19. Cook for about 8–10 minutes, tasting after 8 minutes.

20. Drain when tender but still firm.

Chef's note

The final amount of water depends on egg size; add the last portion only if the dough remains too dry.

instructions:
Culurgiones Dough

Ogliastra pasta filled with potatoes, Pecorino, and mint and sealed in the traditional wheat-ear pattern.

Yield: about 6 servings

Ingredients

For the pasta
1 1/2 cups durum-wheat flour
2/3 cup finely milled semolina
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp plus 1 tsp water
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2/3 tsp fine salt

For the filling
about 6 2/3 cups potatoes
2 cups finely grated Pecorino Sardo
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh mint
1 garlic clove, finely minced
1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil
2/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Boil the potatoes in their skins until completely tender.

2. Drain.

3. Peel while still hot.

4. Mash finely.

5. Cool completely.

6. Add the Pecorino, mint, garlic, olive oil, and salt.

7. Mix into a compact filling.

8. Cover and refrigerate.

9. Mix the durum flour and semolina.

10. Add the salt.

11. Gradually add the water.

12. Add the olive oil.

13. Knead for 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

14. Cover.

15. Rest for 30 minutes.

16. Roll the pasta thin, about 1/16 inch.

17. Cut disks 2 3/4–3 inches wide.

18. Put about 1 tablespoon filling in the center.

19. Lift the edges of the disk.

20. Alternately pinch one side and then the other toward the center to create the traditional wheat-ear closure.

21. Seal the final point completely.

22. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

23. Cook until the culurgiones rise to the surface, about 3–5 minutes.

24. Lift out with a slotted spoon.

Service

Serve with simple tomato sauce and Pecorino or with olive oil and cheese.

Chef's note

The filling should be cold and compact before shaping or the wheat-ear seal becomes difficult to close.

Malloreddus Dough

Sardinian whole-durum semolina pasta ridged on a traditional basket or gnocchi board.

1. Dissolve the salt completely in the water.

14. Drag and curl the dough to create a ridged shell.

title: Lorighittas Dough
instructions:
Lorighittas Dough

Hand-braided Morgongiori pasta made with semolina, water, and salt.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

3 1/2 cups finely milled durum semolina
1 1/4 cups water
1/2 tsp fine salt
3 tbsp semolina for dusting

Preparation

1. Dissolve the salt in the water.

2. Put the semolina in a large bowl.

3. Gradually add the water.

4. Mix by hand.

5. Transfer to a work surface.

6. Knead for at least 15 minutes, until very smooth and elastic.

7. Shape into a disk.

8. Cover in a closed container.

9. Rest for 10 minutes.

10. Pinch off small pieces.

11. Roll into thin strands about 8 inches long.

12. Wrap one strand twice around three fingers.

13. Join the ends firmly.

14. Slide the ring off your fingers.

15. Gently twist the two strands around one another to create the characteristic braid.

16. Arrange on a semolina-dusted towel.

17. Dry for at least 1 hour.

18. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

19. Cook fresh lorighittas for about 5 minutes.

20. Drain.

Service

Dress with chicken ragù, tomato sauce, or another Sardinian sauce.

Chef's note

Seal the ends before twisting the ring so the lorighittas do not open during cooking.

title: Fregola Dough
instructions:
Fregola Dough

Traditional Sardinian durum-semola pasta formed by hand into tiny irregular balls and toasted.

Yield: about 3 cups dried fregola

Ingredients

3 cups medium or fine durum semolina
1 1/4 cups warm water
3/4 tsp fine salt
a generous pinch saffron, optional

Preparation

1. Dissolve the salt in the warm water.

2. Add the saffron if using and let it dissolve.

3. Put 1 tablespoon semolina in a scivedda or large shallow flat-bottomed bowl.

4. Add 1 tablespoon water.

5. Rub the semolina against the bottom with your fingertips and palm in continuous circular motions.

6. Once small clumps begin to form, add another small amount of semolina.

7. Add only a very small amount of water at a time.

8. Continue the circular motion, alternating semolina and water.

9. Stop when the balls reach about 1/16–1/8 inch.

10. Transfer formed balls to a parchment-lined baking sheet.

11. Continue until all semolina and water are used.

12. Air-dry for at least 1 hour; for a drier traditional result, leave until the next day.

13. Preheat the oven to 400°F.

14. Spread the fregola in a single layer.

15. Toast for 15–30 minutes, stirring halfway through.

16. Remove when dry and lightly golden.

17. Cool completely.

Service

Cook in broth or directly in a liquid sauce, risotto-style.

Chef's note

Adding the water by spoonfuls prevents the semolina from becoming one solid dough and lets separate irregular grains form.

Trofie Dough

Liguria semolina pasta tapered and twisted by hand.

11. Place one piece under your palm.

12. Slide it diagonally across the work surface while applying light pressure.

14. Arrange on a semolina-dusted tray.

18. Drain when tender but still firm.

Corzetti Dough

16. Press with the upper stamp to emboss both sides.

17. Arrange on a floured towel.

Pansoti Dough

Mandilli de Saea Dough

Genoese “silk handkerchief” pasta rolled exceptionally thin.

Ingredients

1 1/4 cups type 0 or all-purpose flour
1 egg yolk
1/4 cup plus 2 tsp water

Preparation

2. Make a well in the center.

3. Add the egg yolk.

4. Add the olive oil and salt.

5. Add about 3 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon water.

6. Begin kneading.

title: Tajarin Dough
instructions:
Tajarin Dough

Egg-rich Piedmont pasta rolled paper-thin and cut into extremely fine strands.

2. Make a large well.

4. Add the 4 yolks.

5. Add the salt.

Agnolotti Dough

Piedmont stuffed pasta filled with roast meat, mortadella, and Parmigiano.

Preparation

2. Grind them a second time.

3. Put the meats in a bowl.

4. Add the bread crumbs, Parmigiano, cream, and egg.

5. Add the salt, pepper, and nutmeg.

7. Cover and refrigerate.

8. Make a well in the flour.

18. Place small portions of filling at regular intervals.

19. Fold the pasta over the filling.

24. Cook for 4–6 minutes, until the pasta is tender.

25. Drain gently.

Pizzoccheri Dough

about 3 1/3 cups potatoes

Preparation

5. Continue until compact and uniform.

6. Cover.

7. Rest for 30 minutes.

8. Roll about 1/16–1/8 inch thick.

9. Cut bands 2 3/4–3 inches wide.

10. Stack the bands.

12. Peel the potatoes.

14. Cut the cabbage into pieces.

15. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

16. Add the potatoes.

17. Cook for 5 minutes.

18. Add the cabbage and pizzoccheri.

19. Cook for about 10 minutes.

20. Meanwhile, thinly slice the Casera.

21. Melt the butter with the garlic and rosemary.

22. Let the garlic brown without burning.

23. Lift the pasta and vegetables out with a slotted spoon.

24. Arrange one layer in a warm serving dish.

25. Sprinkle with Casera and Parmigiano.

26. Continue layering.

27. Pour the hot flavored butter over the top.

Serve immediately without excessive mixing.

Chef's note

Warm water helps the buckwheat starches bind and makes the dough easier to roll.

Bigoli Dough

Thick, rough Veneto egg pasta traditionally extruded through a bigolaro press.

1 tbsp plus 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil

1. Sift the flour onto a work surface.

3. Crack the eggs into the center.

4. Add the salt and olive oil.

6. Knead by hand for 10–12 minutes.

8. Cover.

9. Rest for 30 minutes.

10. Divide into pieces sized for the pasta press.

14. Arrange on floured trays.

17. Cook for 6–8 minutes, tasting after 6 minutes.

18. Drain when cooked but still pleasantly chewy.

Dress with duck sauce, anchovy-and-onion sauce, or another Veneto condiment.

Chef's note

The dough should be firmer than tagliatelle dough so the press creates clearly defined rough strands.

instructions:
Potato Gnocchi Dough

Tender potato gnocchi with egg and flour.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 3 1/3 cups potatoes
1 cup all-purpose flour
1 large egg
1 egg yolk
2/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1/2 cup finely grated Parmigiano, optional
1/4 tsp ground nutmeg, optional

Preparation

1. Wash the potatoes.

2. Boil them in their skins for 20–25 minutes, until tender.

3. Drain.

4. Peel while still hot.

5. Rice or mash finely.

6. Cool for 5 minutes.

7. Add the flour, egg, yolk, salt, and pepper.

8. Add the Parmigiano and nutmeg if using.

9. Knead only briefly, just until uniform.

10. Divide into several pieces.

11. Roll into ropes about 3/4 inch thick.

12. Cut into pieces about 3/4 inch long.

13. Ridge each piece on a fork or gnocchi board.

15. Cook only a few at a time.

Roman-style Gnocchi Dough

Roman semolina gnocchi made with milk, egg yolks, butter, and cheese.

Yield: 4 servings

1 1/2 cups semolina
7 tbsp butter, divided
2 egg yolks
1/4 cup finely grated Parmigiano
3 tbsp finely grated Pecorino
1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
2/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Put the milk in a saucepan.

2. Add half of the butter, the salt, and nutmeg.

3. Heat until almost boiling.

4. Slowly rain in the semolina while whisking vigorously.

5. Reduce the heat.

6. Cook, stirring constantly, until very thick and pulling away from the pan.

7. Remove from the heat.

8. Cool for 5 minutes.

9. Mix in the egg yolks.

10. Add the Parmigiano.

11. Stir until uniform.

12. Spread on parchment about 3/8 inch thick.

13. Cool and set.

14. Cut disks 2–2 1/2 inches wide.

15. Butter a baking dish with some of the remaining butter.

16. Arrange the disks slightly overlapping.

17. Dot with the remaining butter.

18. Sprinkle with Pecorino and pepper.

19. Bake in a preheated 400°F oven for 15–20 minutes.

20. Broil for 2–3 minutes.

Service

Chef's note

Add the yolks only after removing the semolina from the heat so they do not scramble.

title: Neapolitan Pizza Dough
instructions:
Neapolitan Pizza Dough

AVPN-style dough made only with flour, water, salt, and fresh yeast.

Yield: about 10–12 dough balls

Ingredients

4 1/4 cups water
3 tbsp fine salt
about 1 tsp fresh yeast
about 14 1/2 cups type 00 or type 0 flour

Preparation

1. Pour the water into a mixer bowl or large mixing bowl.

2. Dissolve the salt in the water.

3. Add about 10% of the flour.

4. Mix into a loose batter.

5. Add the yeast.

6. Continue adding the flour gradually.

7. Knead until smooth, elastic, and nonsticky.

8. Avoid prolonged direct concentrated contact between salt and yeast.

9. Cover the dough.

10. Let it rest in bulk, adjusting for room temperature and flour strength, until fermentation is clearly underway.

11. Divide into dough balls about 1–1 1/4 cups by volume each.

12. Round each into a smooth ball.

13. Put in covered dough boxes.

14. Proof until fully matured.

15. Lightly flour the work surface.

16. Stretch each dough ball only with your hands.

17. Press from the center outward, leaving a 1/2–3/4-inch rim.

18. Do not use a rolling pin.

19. Add toppings.

20. Bake in a very hot pizza oven until the rim is fully risen and char-speckled.

Service

Serve immediately from the oven.

Chef's note

A rolling pin expels fermentation gases and prevents the characteristic cornicione from developing.

title: Genoese Focaccia Dough
instructions:
Genoese Focaccia Dough

Genoese focaccia finished with a water, salt, and olive-oil brine.

Yield: two 12 × 12-inch pans

Ingredients

2 3/4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
1 2/3 cups bread flour
1 cup plus 3 tbsp water
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
about 2 tsp fresh yeast
1 tbsp plus 2 tsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil for the pans

For the brine
3/4 cup water
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in about 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon of the water.

2. Mix the two flours.

3. Gradually add the yeast water.

4. Add some of the remaining water.

5. Begin kneading.

6. Add the salt.

7. Work in the remaining water.

8. Add the olive oil.

9. Knead until smooth.

10. Cover with a bowl.

11. Rest for 15 minutes.

12. Make a series of folds.

13. Rest another 15 minutes.

14. Repeat the folds.

15. Let rise for at least 1 hour.

16. Divide the dough in half.

17. Oil the pans generously.

18. Stretch the dough gently.

19. Rest for 35–40 minutes.

20. Mix the brine water, salt, and olive oil.

21. Press deep dimples with your fingertips.

22. Pour the brine evenly over the surface.

23. Cover.

24. Proof another 45 minutes.

25. Preheat the oven to 400°F.

26. Bake for about 15 minutes.

27. Broil for 3–4 minutes if needed for deeper browning.

Service

Serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

The brine should pool in the characteristic dimples rather than disappear completely before baking.

Barese Focaccia Dough

Bari focaccia with wheat flour, semolina, potato, cherry tomatoes, olives, and oregano.

Yield: one 12 1/2-inch pan

Ingredients

For the dough
2 1/2 cups type 0 or all-purpose flour

about 2/3 cup mashed boiled potato
1 1/2 cups warm water
about 1 tbsp fresh yeast
1 2/3 tsp fine salt

1 tsp granulated sugar

For the top
about 2 2/3 cups cherry tomatoes
20 Bari-style olives

Preparation

1. Boil the potato.

2. Peel it.

3. Mash finely.

4. Mix the flour and semolina.

5. Add the potato.

6. Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm water.

7. Gradually add the liquid to the flours.

8. Knead until the dough begins to come together.

9. Add the salt.

10. Add 2 tablespoons olive oil.

11. Knead for 10–12 minutes, until soft and slightly sticky.

12. Cover.

13. Let rise until doubled, about 2 hours.

14. Generously oil the pan with some of the remaining oil.

15. Transfer the dough to the pan.

16. Stretch gently with oiled fingers.

17. Rest for 30–40 minutes.

18. Halve the cherry tomatoes.

19. Press them lightly into the dough cut-side down.

20. Add the olives.

21. Sprinkle with oregano and coarse salt.

22. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

23. Preheat a conventional oven to 480°F.

24. Bake on a low rack for 18–22 minutes.

25. Broil for about 3 minutes if needed.

Service

Serve hot, warm, or at room temperature.

Chef's note

The dough should remain soft and slightly sticky; adding extra flour reduces the open crumb.

Romagna Piadina Dough

Piadina Romagnola IGP made with flour, lard, water, and salt.

Yield: about 8 flatbreads

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
5 tbsp lard
1 cup plus 1 tbsp water
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp baking soda, optional

Preparation

1. Put the flour on a work surface.

2. Add the salt.

3. Add the baking soda if using.

4. Mix the dry ingredients.

5. Make a well in the center.

6. Add the lard.

7. Soften it with a fork and a small amount of the water.

8. Gradually add the remaining water.

9. Knead for 8–10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

10. Shape into a ball.

11. Cover.

12. Rest for 30 minutes.

13. Divide into 8 equal balls.

14. Roll each ball with a rolling pin.

15. For the classic style, roll about 3/16 inch thick.

16. Heat a testo or heavy griddle to about 400–480°F.

17. Cook one piadina at a time.

18. Pierce any large bubbles with a fork.

19. Turn after about 1–2 minutes.

20. Cook the second side for 1–2 minutes.

21. Keep total cooking time under about 4 minutes.

Chef's note

The goal is amber spotting without drying the flatbread completely.

title: Italian-style Cornetto
instructions:
Italian-style Cornetto

Soft, rich Italian breakfast rolls made with butter, vanilla, and a long-fermented yeast dough.

Yield: about 30 cornetti

Ingredients

about 8 1/3 cups strong bread flour
about 2 large eggs
1/2 cup plus 2 tbsp granulated sugar
1 3/4 cups water
about 3 tbsp fresh yeast
7 tbsp softened butter
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt
1 tbsp malt powder, optional
1 packet vanilla sugar

For brushing
1 large egg
1 tbsp whole milk

Preparation

1. Pour the water into the mixer bowl.

2. Dissolve the yeast in the water.

3. Add the sifted flour.

4. Add the eggs and vanilla.

5. Mix on low speed for about 5 minutes.

6. Add the sugar.

7. Add the malt if using.

8. Continue mixing.

9. Add the salt.

10. Gradually work in the softened butter.

11. Knead for another 5–8 minutes, until smooth, elastic, and well developed.

12. Transfer to a lightly floured work surface.

13. Shape into a ball.

14. Put in a lightly greased bowl.

15. Cover.

16. Let rise for 1 hour at room temperature.

17. Refrigerate for about 12 hours.

18. Return the dough to the work surface.

19. Divide into portions.

20. Roll each portion about 3/16 inch thick.

21. Cut into long narrow triangles.

22. Cut a small slit in the center of each triangle’s base.

23. Gently widen the base.

24. Roll from the base toward the tip without compressing the dough.

25. Arrange on parchment-lined baking sheets with the tips underneath.

26. Cover.

27. Proof until visibly puffy and light, about 1 1/2–2 hours.

28. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

29. Beat the egg with the milk.

30. Brush the cornetti gently.

31. Bake for 15–18 minutes, until evenly golden.

32. Cool on a rack.

Service

Serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

The long refrigerator rest improves flavor and structure and makes the dough easier to shape.

title: Custard-filled Cornetto

Custard-filled Cornetto

Soft yeast cornetti filled with lemon pastry cream.

Yield: 16 cornetti

Ingredients

For the dough
4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
2 large eggs
1/3 cup granulated sugar
4 tbsp softened butter
3/4 cup whole milk
about 2 tbsp fresh yeast

For the lemon cream

1 large egg
3/4 cup plus 2 tbsp granulated sugar
6 tbsp potato starch
finely grated zest of 1 lemon

For brushing
1 large egg

Preparation

1. Warm the milk.

2. Dissolve the yeast in it.

3. Beat the 2 eggs with the sugar.

4. Add the softened butter.

5. Add the yeast milk.

6. Add the salt.

7. Gradually add the flour.

8. Knead for 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

9. Cover.

10. Let rise for at least 2 hours, until doubled.

11. For the cream, put the water, lemon zest, lemon juice, and half of the sugar in a saucepan.

12. Heat until almost boiling.

13. In a bowl, beat the egg with the remaining sugar.

14. Add the potato starch.

15. Mix until smooth.

16. Gradually whisk in the hot liquid.

17. Return everything to the saucepan.

18. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring, until thick.

19. Transfer to a bowl.

20. Cover directly on the surface.

21. Cool completely.

22. Divide the risen dough in half.

23. Roll into two thin disks of equal size.

24. Spread the cold cream over one disk, leaving a 3/8-inch border.

25. Cover with the second disk.

26. Press gently.

27. Cut into 16 triangles.

28. Roll each triangle from the base toward the point.

29. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

30. Cover.

31. Proof for 45–60 minutes.

32. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

33. Beat the egg with the milk.

34. Brush the cornetti.

35. Bake for 18–22 minutes, until golden.

Service

Serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

The cream must be completely cold before filling the dough so it does not interfere with the final rise.

Roman Breakfast Lemon Ring Cake

Light lemon ring cake with oil, vanilla, and whipped egg whites.

Yield: about 12 servings

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

2. Generously butter a 10-inch ring or Bundt pan.

3. Flour the pan.

4. Mix the flour, baking powder, and half of the salt.

5. Put the egg whites in a clean bowl.

6. Add the remaining salt.

8. In a second bowl, rub the sugar with the lemon zest.

9. Add the egg yolks.

10. Beat for 3 minutes.

11. Slowly add the oil while beating.

12. Continue beating for another 3 minutes.

13. Add the lemon juice, vanilla, and optional lemon extract.

14. Mix in the dry ingredients.

15. Fold in one-third of the egg whites to lighten the batter.

17. Pour into the pan.

18. Smooth the surface.

20. Test with a toothpick.

21. Rest in the pan for 5 minutes.

22. Unmold onto a rack.

23. Cool completely.

24. Dust with powdered sugar.

Fold the egg whites gently to preserve the air that gives the cake its height and tenderness.

Soft Italian sweet buns with chocolate chips and vanilla.

instructions:
Brioche Col Tuppo

Soft Sicilian brioche with the characteristic small topknot.

Ingredients

about 1/2 cup egg yolks

Preparation

1. Put the flour, sugar, yeast, milk, vanilla, and lemon zest in the mixer bowl.

2. Add about two-thirds of the egg yolks.

3. Knead until the dough begins to become smooth.

4. Gradually add the lard.

5. Add the remaining yolks.

6. Add the salt.

7. Continue kneading until smooth, elastic, and well developed.

8. Transfer to a lightly greased bowl.

9. Cover.

10. Rest for about 1 hour.

11. Divide into 10 portions for the main buns.

12. Reserve the remaining dough for the topknots.

13. Round the main portions into smooth balls.

14. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

17. Make a deep indentation in the center of each large ball.

18. Insert a topknot.

19. Rest another 30 minutes.

20. Cover.

21. Proof for about 1 more hour, until well puffed.

22. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

23. Beat the egg with the milk.

24. Brush gently.

25. Bake for about 12 minutes, until golden.

26. Cool on a rack.

Service

Chef's note

Make the indentation for the topknot deep enough to keep it attached during proofing and baking.

title: Granita with Brioche
instructions:
Granita with Brioche

Sicilian almond granita served with soft brioche.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

For the granita
1 1/2 cups shelled almonds
2 cups plus 2 tbsp water
3/4 cup granulated sugar

For the brioche
3 1/3 cups bread flour
7 tbsp softened butter
3 large eggs
scant 1/2 cup whole milk
about 1 tbsp fresh yeast
2 tbsp honey
2/3 tsp fine salt

For brushing
1 large egg

Preparation

1. Put the almonds in a blender.

2. Add the water.

3. Blend very finely for 2–3 minutes.

4. Strain through a fine cloth, squeezing thoroughly.

5. Add the sugar to the almond milk.

6. Stir until completely dissolved.

7. Pour into a wide shallow container.

8. Freeze.

9. After 30 minutes, scrape vigorously with a fork.

10. Repeat every 30 minutes for about 3 hours, until fine crystals form.

11. For the brioche, warm the milk.

12. Dissolve the yeast in it.

13. Put the flour, eggs, honey, and yeast milk in a mixer bowl.

14. Knead for 5 minutes.

15. Add the salt.

16. Gradually work in the softened butter.

17. Continue kneading until smooth and elastic.

18. Cover.

19. Let rise for 2 hours.

20. Divide into 6 main portions and 6 small portions for the topknots.

21. Shape into smooth balls.

22. Insert a small topknot into the center of each brioche.

23. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

24. Cover.

25. Proof for 45 minutes.

26. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

27. Beat the egg with the milk.

28. Brush the brioche.

29. Bake for 18–20 minutes.

30. Cool on a rack.

31. Just before serving, scrape the granita again with a fork.

Service

Spoon the granita into chilled glasses or bowls and serve with a brioche alongside.

Chef's note

Frequent stirring during freezing prevents a solid block of ice and keeps the granita fine and fluffy.

Sicilian Iris

Palermo baked brioche pastries filled with sweet sheep’s-milk ricotta and chocolate chips.

Palermo fried spiral pastries filled with sweet ricotta cream.

3. Press through a sieve.

4. Add the sugar.

5. Mix until smooth.

6. Fold in the chocolate chips.

7. Refrigerate.

8. Warm the milk.

9. Dissolve the yeast in it.

10. Put the flour and sugar in a bowl.

11. Add the yeast milk.

12. Add the lard.

13. Begin kneading.

14. Add the salt.

15. Continue until smooth and compact.

18. Divide into portions.

19. Shape into balls.

24. Arrange on a tray.

25. Cover.

26. Proof for about 1 hour.

27. Heat the oil to 340°F.

28. Fry one pastry at a time for 3–4 minutes, turning until evenly golden.

29. Drain on paper towels.

30. Cool until warm.

31. Carefully remove the metal forms.

32. Fill with the ricotta cream.

Preparation

1. Put the flour and cool but pliable lard in a large bowl.

2. Work quickly until sandy.

3. Dissolve the sugar and salt in the water.

4. Gradually add the liquid to the flour mixture.

5. Mix only until the dough comes together.

6. Do not overwork.

12. Roll each portion about 3/16 inch thick.

title: Breakfast Sfogliatella Riccia
instructions:
Breakfast Sfogliatella Riccia

Neapolitan laminated pastry with lard and a semolina, ricotta, citron, and citrus filling.

Yield: 14–16 pastries

Ingredients

For the pastry
4 cups plus 2 tbsp strong all-purpose flour
2/3 cup plus 2 tsp warm water
2 tsp honey
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 1/3 cups softened lard

For the filling
1 1/4 cups well-drained sheep’s-milk ricotta
2/3 cup fine semolina
1 1/2 cups water
1 cup granulated sugar
2 large eggs
1 egg yolk
about 1/3 cup diced candied citron
1 tsp ground cinnamon
1 vial orange-flower water
finely grated zest of 1 orange
1/3 tsp fine salt

For finishing
1 large egg
1/3 cup powdered sugar

Preparation

1. Dissolve the honey and salt in the warm water.

2. Put the flour in a large bowl.

3. Gradually add the water.

4. Knead for 10–12 minutes, until smooth and very elastic.

5. Cover.

6. Rest for 30 minutes.

7. Divide into portions.

8. Roll each portion extremely thin, almost transparent.

9. Brush each sheet with softened lard.

10. Stack or join the sheets in the direction of lamination.

11. Roll very tightly into a compact cylinder.

12. Wrap.

13. Refrigerate for at least 8 hours, preferably overnight.

14. For the filling, bring the water, sugar, and salt to a boil.

15. Slowly add the semolina.

16. Cook for 5–7 minutes, stirring.

17. Cool completely.

18. Add the ricotta, eggs, yolk, citron, cinnamon, orange-flower water, and orange zest.

19. Mix until uniform.

20. Cut the pastry roll into slices 3/8–1/2 inch thick.

21. Use your thumbs to gently push the center of each slice outward into a shell.

22. Put about 2 tablespoons filling inside.

23. Close without compressing the laminated edges.

24. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

25. Preheat a conventional oven to 400°F.

26. Beat the egg.

27. Brush lightly.

28. Bake for 20–25 minutes, until deeply golden and crisp.

29. Rest for 5 minutes.

30. Dust with powdered sugar.

Service

Serve warm.

Chef's note

Do not compress the laminated edges while shaping; the layers need room to open in the oven.

title: Polacca Aversana
instructions:
Polacca Aversana

Aversa yeast cake filled with pastry cream and sour cherries.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

For the dough
1 1/4 cups bread flour
1 cup type 0 or all-purpose flour
scant 1/2 cup whole milk

For the pastry cream

1/2 vanilla bean

For the filling
about 2/3 cup drained sour cherries in syrup

For finishing
1 egg yolk
1 tbsp whole milk

Preparation

1. Prepare the pastry cream.

2. Heat the milk with the vanilla.

3. In a bowl, beat the egg yolks with the sugar.

4. Add the flour or cornstarch.

5. Gradually whisk in the hot milk.

6. Return to the heat.

7. Cook, stirring, until thick.

8. Transfer to a bowl.

9. Cover directly on the surface.

10. Cool completely.

11. For the dough, mix the two flours.

12. Add the sugar, salt, and lemon zest.

13. Add the yeast, egg, and milk.

14. Knead for 5–6 minutes.

15. Gradually work in the softened butter.

16. Continue kneading until smooth and nonsticky.

17. Cover.

18. Let rise for 2–3 hours, until doubled.

19. Divide the dough in half.

20. Roll into two equal disks.

21. Put the first disk into a 9 1/2-inch pan.

22. Spread the cold pastry cream, leaving a 3/4-inch border.

23. Scatter the sour cherries over the cream.

24. Cover with the second disk.

25. Seal the edges firmly.

26. Cover.

27. Proof for 45–60 minutes.

28. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

29. Mix the egg yolk and milk.

30. Brush the surface.

31. Sprinkle with pearl sugar.

32. Bake for about 30 minutes, until golden.

33. Cool before slicing.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

The pastry cream should be cold and firm before it is enclosed in the yeast dough.

Neapolitan Brioche Braid

Soft milk brioche braid flavored with lemon and vanilla and topped with pearl sugar.

Preparation

2. Dissolve the yeast in it.

3. Put the flour and sugar in a large bowl.

6. Add the lemon zest and vanilla.

7. Gradually add the yeast milk.

8. Add the salt.

9. Knead for 10–12 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

10. Shape into a ball.

11. Cover.

12. Let rise until doubled, about 2 hours.

13. Divide the dough into three equal portions.

14. Roll into three long even ropes.

15. Join the top ends.

16. Braid without pulling too tightly.

17. Seal the lower ends.

18. Transfer to a parchment-lined baking sheet.

19. Cover.

20. Proof for 45–60 minutes.

21. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

22. Mix the egg yolk and milk.

23. Brush the braid.

24. Sprinkle with pearl sugar.

25. Bake for about 30 minutes.

26. If the top becomes too dark, loosely cover with foil during the final 10 minutes.

27. Cool on a rack.

Braid loosely so the three strands have room to expand during the final proof.

Puglian Friselle

Salento durum-semolina rings baked twice until dry and crisp.

Yield: 16 friselle

Ingredients

3 cups finely milled durum semolina
1 1/4 cups water, room temperature
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
about 1 tsp fresh yeast
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons water.

2. Put the semolina in a large bowl.

3. Add the yeast water.

4. Knead for 3–4 minutes.

5. Dissolve the salt in the remaining water.

6. Gradually add the salted water.

7. Add the olive oil.

8. Knead for about 10 minutes by hand or 8 minutes in a mixer, until smooth.

9. Shape into a ball.

10. Cover.

11. Rest for 1 hour.

12. Divide into 8 equal pieces.

13. Roll into ropes about 8–9 inches long.

14. Join each rope into a ring.

15. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

16. Cover.

17. Proof for 1–1 1/2 hours, until nearly doubled.

18. Preheat a conventional oven to 425°F.

19. Bake for 20–25 minutes.

20. Remove from the oven.

21. Wait 5 minutes.

22. Cut each ring horizontally in half with a serrated knife or strong thread.

23. Arrange the 16 halves cut-side up.

24. Reduce a convection oven to 300°F.

25. Bake for another 35–45 minutes, until completely dry.

26. Cool on a rack.

Service

Chef's note

The second bake should remove nearly all moisture, which is what gives friselle their long shelf life.

Pittanchiusa

Calabrian Christmas pastry made from spirals filled with walnuts, almonds, raisins, and spices.

Pardulas

Seadas

Roll the pastry thin and seal it firmly so the cheese melts without escaping into the oil.

Sardinian sweet almond, egg, and butter focaccia.

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 400°F.

2. Cover the almonds with boiling water.

3. Rest for 3 minutes.

4. Drain.

5. Remove the skins.

6. Spread the almonds on a baking sheet.

7. Dry in the oven for 5 minutes without browning.

8. Cool.

9. Grind finely.

10. Put the flour on a work surface.

11. Make a well.

12. Add the ground almonds, eggs, about 3 tablespoons butter, sugar, and salt.

13. Knead by hand for 10–12 minutes, until firm and elastic.

14. Butter a roughly 12 × 16-inch pan with the remaining butter.

instructions:
Milanese Michetta

Light hollow Milanese bread made with a long-fermented biga.

Yield: about 20–25 rolls

Ingredients

For the biga
about 12 1/2 cups strong bread flour
3 cups plus 3 tbsp water
about 2 tbsp fresh yeast

For the final dough
1 1/4 cups strong bread flour
2/3 cup water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt
1 tbsp malt powder

Preparation

1. Mix the biga flour, water, and yeast only until no dry flour remains.

2. Do not knead to full gluten development.

3. Cover.

4. Ferment for at least 18 hours at about 54°F.

5. Tear the biga into pieces in the mixer bowl.

6. Add the final-dough water.

7. Add the salt and malt.

8. Mix vigorously for 1 minute.

9. Add the remaining flour.

10. Mix for 10 minutes on low speed.

11. Continue for 5 minutes on the next speed.

12. Transfer to the work surface.

13. Cover.

14. Rest for 5 minutes.

15. Give the dough a series of folds.

16. Rest for 10–15 minutes.

17. Shape into an even cylinder.

18. Lightly oil the surface.

19. Rest for 20 minutes.

20. Divide into equal portions.

21. Round each piece.

22. Stamp with the traditional star-shaped michetta press.

23. Place stamped-side down on a floured cloth.

24. Cover with food-safe plastic.

25. Rest for 30 minutes.

26. Preheat the oven to 480°F with strong steam available at the beginning of the bake.

27. Turn the rolls stamped-side up onto the baking surface.

28. Bake until fully puffed, golden, and lightly browned.

29. Cool on a rack.

Service

Serve as fresh as possible.

Chef's note

The long biga fermentation and strong initial steam create the characteristic hollow center.

Breakfast Torta Paradiso

Pavia butter-and-lemon cake with a light, delicate crumb.

1/3 tsp fine salt

2 tbsp flour for the pan
1/4 cup powdered sugar for finishing

1. Preheat the oven to 340°F.

2. Butter and flour an 8 1/2–9 1/2-inch cake pan.

3. Beat the softened butter with the sugar and lemon zest.

4. Continue until very pale and fluffy.

5. Add the egg yolks one at a time.

6. Beat the egg whites with the salt to stiff peaks.

7. Sift together the flour, potato starch, and baking powder.

8. Mix the dry ingredients into the butter mixture.

9. Fold in one-third of the egg whites to lighten the batter.

10. Gently fold in the remaining whites.

11. Pour into the pan.

12. Smooth the surface.

13. Bake for 45–60 minutes.

14. Test with a toothpick after 45 minutes.

15. Cool in the pan for 10 minutes.

16. Unmold.

17. Cool completely on a rack.

18. Dust with powdered sugar.

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Thoroughly creaming the butter and sugar and gently folding the whites creates the cake’s fine airy crumb.

Kranz

Layered brioche-and-puff-pastry twists with apricot preserves, raisins, and candied orange.

2 1/2 cups strong bread flour
about 1 tsp fresh yeast

Preparation

1. Mix the honey, rum, vanilla, and citrus zest.

2. Put the flour, yeast, milk, and sugar in a mixer bowl.

3. Knead for 3–4 minutes.

4. Add the eggs one at a time.

5. Work in the softened butter in three additions.

6. Add the salt and aromatic mixture.

7. Knead until fully developed.

8. Shape into a ball.

9. Cover.

10. Let rise until doubled.

12. Drain and dry.

13. Roll the brioche and puff pastry into matching rectangles.

14. Spread a thin layer of apricot preserves over the brioche.

15. Scatter half of the raisins and candied orange over it.

16. Cover with the puff pastry.

17. Spread another thin layer of preserves and the remaining fruit.

18. Fold or layer according to the traditional shape.

19. Transfer to a parchment-lined tray.

20. Refrigerate for 1 hour.

22. Twist each strip gently.

23. Arrange on a baking sheet.

27. Mix the egg yolk and milk.

28. Brush the pastries.

Chilling before cutting makes the brioche, puff-pastry, and filling layers more distinct.

Buchteln

Soft South Tyrolean pull-apart buns filled with jam.

Yield: about 12 buns

1 packet vanilla sugar
2 tbsp butter, divided
1 tbsp rum

2. Cover.

3. Let activate for 20 minutes at about 95°F.

4. Melt about 1 1/2 tablespoons butter.

5. Mix it with the eggs, remaining sugar, vanilla sugar, salt, and rum.

6. Sift the flour into a large bowl.

7. Add the yeast mixture.

8. Add the egg mixture.

9. Knead vigorously until smooth and visibly aerated.

10. Cover.

11. Let rise for another 20 minutes.

12. Roll the dough about 3/8 inch thick.

13. Cut disks about 3 inches wide.

14. Put about 1 tablespoon jam in the center.

15. Close into balls.

16. Melt the remaining butter.

17. Brush each ball.

19. Cover.

22. Bake for about 30 minutes, until golden.

Brushing the sides with butter lets the buns separate easily after baking while keeping them soft.

8. Gradually add the egg mixture.

9. Work only until the dough is firm and uniform.

Work the dough quickly so the butter stays cool and the sugar does not leak during baking.

Esse di Raveo

Friulian butter-and-vanilla cookies shaped into their characteristic S.

Yield: about 25 cookies

Preparation

2. Beat until soft and creamy.

3. Lightly beat the egg with a fork.

4. Add it gradually to the butter mixture.

5. Let each addition absorb before adding more.

7. Mix briefly only until fully absorbed.

8. Flatten the dough.

9. Wrap in plastic.

13. Roll each piece into a rope.

16. Flatten slightly.

The long cold rest makes the dough easier to shape and helps the cookies hold their form while baking.

Breakfast Gubana

Friulian spiral sweet bread from the Natisone Valleys with walnuts, hazelnuts, pine nuts, raisins, cookies, and rum.

Yield: 1 large gubana

Ingredients

For the dough
2 cups plus 1 tbsp all-purpose flour

2 tbsp grappa
scant 1/2 cup whole milk

about 2 cups finely crushed dry cookies or amaretti
1/4 cup rum
finely grated zest of 1 lemon
finely grated zest of 1 orange

For finishing
1 egg white
2 tbsp granulated sugar

Preparation

1. The night before, put the raisins in a bowl with the rum and citrus zest.

2. Cover.

3. Refrigerate overnight.

4. Chop the walnuts and hazelnuts.

5. Toast the pine nuts.

6. Finely crush the cookies.

7. Mix everything with the raisins and rum.

8. Refrigerate the filling until the next day.

9. Beat the egg, softened butter, sugar, grappa, and milk.

10. Mix the two flours with the yeast.

11. Gradually add the liquid mixture.

12. Add the salt last.

13. Knead until smooth and elastic.

14. Shape into a ball.

15. Cover.

16. Let rise for about 3 hours.

17. Roll the dough into a disk about 3/16 inch thick.

18. Spread the filling evenly, leaving a 3/8-inch border.

19. Roll tightly.

20. Coil the roll into a spiral.

21. Transfer to a parchment-lined baking sheet.

22. Cover.

23. Proof for 2 hours.

24. Preheat a conventional oven to 400°F.

25. Brush with egg white.

26. Sprinkle with the sugar.

27. Rest for 10 minutes.

28. Bake for 15 minutes at 400°F.

29. Reduce the oven to 350°F.

30. Continue baking for 15–20 minutes.

31. Cool completely on a rack.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

The overnight filling rest lets the rum and citrus evenly perfume the dried fruit and nuts.

Genoese Sweet Focaccia

Rich Genoese sweet focaccia with raisins, pine nuts, candied fruit, fennel, and Cognac.

Yield: 10–12 servings

2. Drain and dry.

3. Dissolve half of the yeast in 1/2 cup warm water.

5. Cover.

6. Let rise until doubled.

7. Dissolve the remaining yeast in the remaining water.

8. Add the remaining flour, yeast water, butter, eggs, sugar, and salt to the first dough.

9. Knead until uniform.

10. Add the raisins, pine nuts, candied fruit, fennel seeds, lemon zest, and Cognac.

11. Work until evenly distributed.

12. Cover.

13. Let rise until doubled.

14. Preheat the oven to 300°F.

15. Butter and flour an 11-inch round pan.

16. Turn the dough onto the work surface.

17. Knead briefly.

18. Transfer to the pan.

19. Rest for about 15 minutes.

20. Bake for about 1 hour, until deeply golden and baked through.

Dry the raisins thoroughly so they do not add uneven moisture to the rich dough.

Breakfast Pandolce Genovese

Traditional tall Genoese sweet bread with raisins, dried muscat grapes, pine nuts, citron, and fennel.

2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour

2/3 cup dried muscat grapes

about 2/3 cup diced candied citron
1/3 cup fennel seeds
1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Make a well in the first portion of flour.

2. Dissolve the yeast in the warm water.

3. Pour it into the center.

4. Knead until firm and elastic.

5. Put in a bowl.

6. Cover.

7. Let rise in a warm place overnight.

8. The next day, soak the raisins and dried muscat grapes in warm water for 15 minutes.

9. Drain and dry.

10. Dice the candied citron.

11. Melt the butter.

12. Cool slightly.

13. Put the remaining flour in a large bowl.

14. Add the butter, water-and-orange-flower mixture, sugar, and salt.

15. Add the risen first dough.

16. Knead vigorously.

17. Add the raisins, muscat grapes, pine nuts, citron, and fennel seeds.

18. Knead for at least 15 minutes.

19. Divide in half.

20. Shape two domes.

21. Put on two parchment-lined baking sheets.

22. Cut a triangular slash into the top of each loaf.

23. Support each loaf with a cloth or baking collar.

24. Cover.

25. Let rise for another 12 hours.

26. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

27. Bake for about 1 hour, until deeply golden-brown.

28. Cool completely on a rack.

Serve at room temperature.

The two very long rises develop the traditional aroma and texture of tall pandolce.

Breakfast Umbrian Torcolo

Torcolo di San Costanzo with candied citron, raisins, pine nuts, and anise.

2. Drain and squeeze dry.

3. Dissolve the yeast in some of the water.

5. Gradually add the yeast water and remaining water.

6. Add the salt.

7. Knead into a bread-like dough.

8. Cover.

9. Let rise until doubled.

10. Turn onto the work surface.

11. Add the olive oil and sugar.

12. Add the citron, raisins, pine nuts, and anise seeds.

13. Knead for at least 10 minutes.

14. Shape into a ring.

15. Butter and flour a baking pan.

16. Put the ring in the pan.

17. Cover.

18. Proof in a warm place for 2–3 hours.

19. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

20. Separate the egg.

21. Beat the yolk.

22. Brush the surface.

24. Bake for at least 40–45 minutes.

25. Cool on a rack.

instructions:
Pane di Altamura

Altamura DOP bread made with durum semolina, natural starter, water, and sea salt.

Yield: 1 large loaf

Ingredients

6 cups finely milled durum semolina
about 1 1/2 cups active natural starter
2 1/2 cups water at about 64°F
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine sea salt

Preparation

1. Refresh the natural starter at least three times before mixing the dough.

2. Put the semolina in the mixer bowl.

3. Add the natural starter.

4. Gradually add about 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons water.

5. Begin kneading.

6. Dissolve the salt in the remaining water.

7. Gradually add the salted water.

8. Knead with a diving-arm mixer for about 20 minutes, or work by hand until smooth, elastic, and well developed.

9. Cover with a cotton cloth.

10. Rest for at least 90 minutes.

11. Turn onto the work surface.

12. Weigh and shape the loaf by hand.

13. Rest for 30 minutes.

14. Reshape gently.

15. Rest for at least another 15 minutes.

16. Preheat the oven to 480°F.

17. Load the loaf.

18. Bake the first 15 minutes with the oven vented or the door slightly open according to the traditional method.

19. Close the oven.

20. Continue baking for another 45 minutes.

21. Vent the oven during the final 5 minutes to dry the crust.

22. Remove from the oven.

23. Cool completely on a rack before slicing.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

High hydration and long fermentation are essential for the thick crust and aromatic crumb.

title: Pane di Laterza
instructions:
Pane di Laterza

Large Puglian durum-semolina loaf with a resilient crumb and robust crust.

Yield: 1 large loaf

Ingredients

4 1/4 cups finely milled durum semolina
2 cups water, room temperature
1 1/2 tsp active dry yeast
2 1/4 tsp fine salt
1 tsp honey
3 tbsp semolina for dusting

Preparation

1. Pour about 1 3/4 cups water into a large bowl.

2. Add the yeast and honey.

3. Stir until dissolved.

4. Gradually add the semolina.

5. Knead until the dough begins to develop.

6. Dissolve the salt in the remaining water.

7. Gradually add the salted water.

8. Knead for 10–12 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

9. Shape into a ball.

10. Cover.

11. Let rise for about 3 hours.

12. Transfer to a semolina-dusted work surface.

13. Give the dough a series of folds.

14. Rest for 15 minutes.

15. Repeat the folds.

16. Shape into one large loaf.

17. Put on a cloth or in a proofing basket dusted generously with semolina.

18. Cover.

19. Proof for 60–90 minutes.

20. Preheat a conventional oven to 465°F for at least 30 minutes with a baking stone or heavy sheet and a metal steam pan.

21. Turn the loaf onto the baking surface.

22. Score the top.

23. Add hot water to the steam pan.

24. Bake for 15 minutes at 465°F.

25. Remove the steam pan.

26. Reduce the oven to 410°F.

27. Bake another 30–40 minutes.

28. Leave the oven door slightly open during the final 5 minutes.

29. Cool on a rack for at least 2 hours.

Service

Slice only after completely cooling.

Chef's note

The long cooling period lets the highly hydrated crumb stabilize before slicing.

Pane di Monte Sant’angelo

Large Gargano loaf made with type 0 flour, water, salt, and natural starter.

Yield: 1 large loaf

Ingredients

8 1/3 cups type 0 or all-purpose flour
about 2 cups active natural starter
3 1/3 cups water
1 tbsp plus 1 1/2 tsp fine salt
1/4 cup flour for dusting

Preparation

1. Put the flour in a large bowl.

2. Tear the natural starter into pieces.

3. Add it to the flour.

4. Add about 3 cups water.

5. Mix until a dough forms.

6. Dissolve the salt in the remaining water.

7. Gradually work in the salted water.

8. Knead until smooth, uniform, and highly elastic.

9. Cover.

10. Let rise for about 4 hours.

11. Dust the work surface with flour.

12. Turn out the dough.

13. Fold the outer edges toward the center.

14. Shape into a large round loaf.

15. Put into a well-floured container or proofing basket.

16. Cover.

17. Proof for another 2 hours.

18. Preheat a conventional oven to 445°F.

19. Turn the loaf onto a baking sheet or stone.

20. Bake for about 1 hour 20 minutes.

21. Check that the crust is deeply golden and the base sounds hollow.

22. Cool upright or on a rack so moisture can escape.

Serve only after completely cooling.

The large loaf size and long bake help this bread stay fragrant for many days.

title: Puccia Salentina
instructions:
Puccia Salentina

Classic Salento bread rolls, soft inside and crisp outside.

Yield: about 10 rolls

Ingredients

8 1/3 cups all-purpose flour
scant 2 cups warm water
1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil
about 1 tsp fresh yeast
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil for the surface

Preparation

1. Sift the flour into a large bowl.

2. Gradually add the olive oil.

3. Dissolve the yeast in the warm water.

4. Gradually add the yeast water.

5. Knead until the dough begins to develop gluten.

6. Add the salt.

7. Continue kneading until completely smooth.

8. Transfer to a lightly oiled work surface.

9. Knead briefly again.

10. Put in a lightly oiled bowl.

11. Cover.

12. Let rise for at least 3 hours.

13. Turn onto a lightly floured surface.

14. Divide into equal portions.

15. Shape into balls.

16. Roll each into a disk about 3/16 inch thick.

17. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

18. Brush with the finishing olive oil.

20. Bake for about 20 minutes, until puffed and golden.

Chef's note

Good gluten development helps the rolls puff while keeping the crumb soft and strong enough for fillings.

Puccia Leccese

about 2 tsp fresh yeast

1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil for brushing

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in 3 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon warm water taken from the total.

2. Mix the two flours.

3. Make a well in a large bowl.

4. Add the dissolved yeast.

5. Begin kneading.

6. Gradually add the remaining water.

7. Add the salt.

8. Add the olive oil.

9. Knead until smooth and uniform.

10. Cover.

11. Let rise for at least 2 hours, until doubled.

12. Divide into 4 portions.

13. Shape into smooth balls.

14. Cover.

15. Proof for another 45 minutes.

16. Flatten each ball slightly without fully deflating it.

17. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

18. Brush with the remaining olive oil.

19. Preheat a convection oven to its highest setting.

20. Reduce to 425°F when loading the rolls.

21. Bake for about 15 minutes, until puffed and golden.

Service

Cool until warm, split, and fill.

Chef's note

Do not flatten the proofed dough excessively during final shaping or it will lose its fermentation gases.

Uliata Salentina

Salento bread rolls with black olives kneaded directly into the dough.

4. Gradually add the remaining water.

5. Add the olive oil.

6. Add the salt.

7. Knead for 10–12 minutes.

8. Work in the black olives.

12. Turn onto the work surface.

Puddica Pugliese

Salento focaccia topped with cherry tomatoes, capers, and oregano.

Preparation

2. Dissolve the yeast and sugar in it.

3. Add about 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon flour.

4. Mix.

5. Ferment for about 20 minutes.

6. Make a well in the remaining flour.

7. Add the starter.

8. Gradually add the remaining water.

9. Add the olive oil.

10. Add the salt.

11. Knead until smooth and firm.

12. Cover.

13. Let rise for about 1 hour.

14. Grease a baking pan with half of the topping olive oil.

15. Roll or stretch the dough about 3/16 inch thick.

16. Put it in the pan.

17. Quarter the cherry tomatoes.

18. Scatter them over the surface.

19. Add the capers.

20. Sprinkle with the oregano and salt.

21. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

22. Cover.

23. Proof for another 30 minutes.

The second proof with the topping in place lets the tomato juices perfume the surface without soaking the base.

Puglian Potato Focaccia

Puglian focaccia with potato in the dough and rosemary.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

6 2/3 cups type 0 or all-purpose flour
about 1 2/3 cups boiled potatoes, divided
about 1 tbsp fresh yeast

5 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
2 tsp fine salt

1. Boil the potatoes until tender.

2. Drain and peel.

3. Mash half of the potatoes.

4. Slice the remaining potatoes.

5. Dissolve the yeast in 1 cup warm water.

6. Make a well in the flour.

7. Add the mashed potatoes.

8. Add the dissolved yeast.

9. Gradually add the remaining water.

10. Add 2 tablespoons olive oil.

11. Add the fine salt.

12. Knead until soft and smooth.

13. Cover.

14. Let rise for 1 hour.

15. Mix the sliced potatoes with the egg.

16. Add the rosemary, pepper, and 1 tablespoon olive oil.

17. Preheat the oven to 300°F.

18. Grease a baking pan with 1 tablespoon olive oil.

19. Stretch the dough into a round.

20. Spread the potato mixture over the top.

title: Puglian Friselle
instructions:
Puglian Friselle

Durum-semolina rings made with liquid sourdough starter and baked twice until completely dry.

Yield: 18 half-friselle

Ingredients

3 cups finely milled durum semolina
1 1/4 cups water
about 1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp active liquid sourdough starter
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1 2/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Put the semolina in a large bowl.

2. Add about 1 cup plus 1 tablespoon water.

3. Mix for about 3 minutes, until all of the semolina is hydrated.

4. Cover.

5. Rest for 60 minutes.

6. Add the liquid starter.

7. Knead for about 4 minutes.

8. Cover.

9. Rest for 15 minutes.

10. Dissolve the salt in the remaining 3 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon water.

11. Gradually work in the salted water.

12. Add the olive oil.

13. Knead until smooth and elastic.

14. Cover.

15. Let rise until doubled.

16. Divide into 9 equal pieces.

17. Shape into balls.

18. Rest for 10 minutes.

19. Roll each ball into a rope.

20. Join the ends to form a ring.

21. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

22. Cover.

23. Proof for about 1 hour.

24. Preheat a conventional oven to 410°F.

25. Bake for about 20 minutes.

26. Remove from the oven.

27. While still hot, cut each ring horizontally in half.

28. Reduce the oven to 320°F.

29. Arrange the halves cut-side up.

30. Bake again until completely dry and crisp, about 35–45 minutes.

31. Cool completely on a rack.

Service

Briefly soak in water before topping.

Chef's note

The second bake should remove nearly all moisture to create the traditional crisp texture and long keeping quality.

title: Puglian Taralli
instructions:
Puglian Taralli

Puglian white-wine and olive-oil rings, boiled before baking.

Yield: about 50 taralli

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1/2 cup dry white wine
2 1/2 tsp fine salt
2 tsp fennel seeds

Preparation

1. Put the flour, salt, and fennel seeds in a large bowl.

2. Mix.

3. Add the olive oil.

4. Add the wine.

5. Knead for 8–10 minutes, until smooth and compact.

6. Cover.

7. Rest for 30 minutes.

8. Divide into small pieces.

9. Roll into ropes about 3/8 inch thick and 3–4 inches long.

10. Join the ends into rings.

11. Bring a large pot of water to a boil.

12. Add only a few taralli at a time.

13. Lift them out with a slotted spoon as soon as they float.

14. Arrange on a clean kitchen towel.

15. Dry for at least 2 hours.

16. Preheat a conventional oven to 375°F.

17. Arrange the taralli on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

18. Bake for 20–25 minutes, until golden and completely dry.

19. Cool on a rack.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Drying after boiling is important because it makes the taralli crisp rather than rubbery.

title: Pane di Matera
instructions:
Pane di Matera

Matera bread made with durum semolina, natural starter, and long fermentation.

Yield: 1 large loaf

Ingredients

6 cups finely milled durum semolina
about 2 cups active refreshed natural starter
2 3/4 cups warm water
1 tbsp plus 2 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Refresh the natural starter until fully active.

2. Dissolve it in about 2 1/3 cups warm water.

3. Put the semolina in a large bowl.

4. Gradually add the starter water.

5. Knead for 8–10 minutes.

6. Dissolve the salt in the remaining scant 1/2 cup water.

7. Gradually work in the salted water.

8. Continue kneading until smooth, elastic, and well developed.

9. Cover with a damp cloth.

10. Let rise in a warm place for 3–4 hours, until doubled.

11. Turn the dough onto a lightly semolina-dusted work surface.

12. Deflate gently.

13. Shape into the traditional tall or horn-shaped loaf.

14. Cover.

15. Proof for about 1 hour.

16. Preheat a conventional oven to 480°F.

17. Load the loaf.

18. Bake for 15 minutes at 480°F.

19. Reduce the oven to 350°F.

20. Continue baking for 45–50 minutes.

21. Check that the base sounds hollow.

22. Cool completely on a rack before slicing.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Cool the loaf completely so the highly hydrated crumb can set before slicing.

title: Strazzata Lucana
instructions:
Strazzata Lucana

Lucanian peppered bread rings with extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 2 rings

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp type 0 or all-purpose flour
1 1/4 cups water
about 2 tsp fresh yeast
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in the water.

2. Put the flour in a large bowl.

3. Gradually add the yeast water.

4. Knead until the dough begins to become uniform.

5. Add the salt.

6. Add the pepper.

7. Add about 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon olive oil.

8. Knead for 8–10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

9. Cover.

10. Let rise for about 1 hour.

11. Divide the dough in half.

12. Shape into two ropes.

13. Join the ends of each rope to make a ring.

14. Arrange on parchment-lined baking sheets.

15. Cover.

16. Proof for another 30 minutes.

17. Preheat the oven to 465°F.

18. Brush with the remaining olive oil.

19. Bake for 10–15 minutes, until well puffed and golden.

20. Cool slightly on a rack.

Service

Serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

The black pepper should be clearly noticeable but evenly distributed throughout the dough.

instructions:
Matera Focaccia with Cherry Tomatoes and Oregano

Soft Lucanian focaccia topped with cherry tomatoes, oregano, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: one 12 × 16-inch pan

Ingredients

For the dough
4 cups plus 2 tbsp type 0 or all-purpose flour
1 1/2 cups warm water
2 1/4 tsp active dry yeast or about 1 1/2 tbsp fresh yeast
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp granulated sugar
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

For the top
2 cups cherry tomatoes
2 tbsp plus 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 tsp dried oregano
2/3 tsp fine salt
1/3 tsp coarse salt, optional

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in the warm water with the sugar.

2. Put the flour in a large bowl.

3. Gradually add the yeast water.

4. Add the olive oil.

5. Add the salt.

6. Knead for 8–10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

7. Cover.

8. Let rise until doubled, about 1 1/2–2 hours.

9. Lightly oil a 12 × 16-inch pan with some of the topping oil.

10. Transfer the dough to the pan.

11. Gently stretch with your fingers.

12. Rest for 30 minutes.

13. Halve the cherry tomatoes.

14. Press them lightly into the dough.

15. Scatter the oregano over the top.

16. Add the fine salt and optional coarse salt.

17. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

18. Preheat a conventional oven to 425°F.

19. Bake for 25–30 minutes, until the base is baked and the top golden.

20. Rest in the pan for 5 minutes.

21. Transfer to a rack.

22. Rest another 10–15 minutes before cutting.

Service

Serve hot, warm, or at room temperature.

Chef's note

Brief rack cooling prevents residual steam from softening the bottom crust.

title: Pane di Trecchina
instructions:
Pane di Trecchina

Lucanian naturally leavened bread made with the traditional criscito starter.

Yield: 1 large loaf

Ingredients

8 1/3 cups type 00 or all-purpose flour
about 2 cups active natural starter, preferably traditional criscito
2 3/4 cups water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Refresh the natural starter until highly active.

2. Put the flour in a large bowl.

3. Tear the starter into pieces.

4. Add it to the flour.

5. Add about 2 1/3 cups water.

6. Knead for 10 minutes.

7. Dissolve the salt in the remaining scant 1/2 cup water.

8. Gradually work in the salted water.

9. Continue kneading until smooth, elastic, and well developed.

10. Shape into a large ball.

11. Cover.

12. Ferment slowly for at least 8–12 hours in a cool room, until clearly expanded.

13. Turn onto a floured work surface.

14. Shape into a broad round loaf.

15. Put into a floured proofing basket or on a floured cloth.

16. Cover.

17. Proof for another 2–3 hours.

18. Preheat the oven with a baking stone or heavy sheet to 465°F.

19. Turn the loaf onto the baking surface.

20. Score the top with a cross, triangle, or square.

21. Bake for 20 minutes at 465°F.

22. Reduce the oven to 400°F.

23. Continue baking for 45–55 minutes.

24. Vent the oven during the final 10 minutes.

25. Cool completely on a rack.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Very long natural fermentation develops the mild sweetness and resilient crumb associated with Trecchina bread.

title: Pane di Cerchiara
instructions:
Pane di Cerchiara

Large Calabrian naturally leavened loaf made with soft-wheat flour and a whole-grain component.

Yield: 1 large loaf

Ingredients

5 cups type 0 or all-purpose flour
3 1/3 cups whole-wheat flour
3 cups water at about 64–68°F
about 1 1/2 cups active natural starter
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Refresh the natural starter on the day of baking.

2. Mix the type 0 and whole-wheat flours.

3. Tear the starter into pieces.

4. Add it to the flours.

5. Add about 2 1/2 cups water.

6. Knead for 15 minutes.

7. Dissolve the salt in the remaining scant 1/2 cup water.

8. Gradually work in the salted water.

9. Continue kneading for 20–25 minutes total, until uniform and soft to the touch.

10. Cover.

11. Let rise naturally for at least 6 hours.

12. Turn onto a lightly floured surface.

13. Shape into a large round loaf.

14. Fold one side of the dough over itself to create the traditional raised rasella.

15. Put on a floured cloth.

16. Cover.

17. Complete the proof for about 1 hour.

18. Preheat the oven as hot as practical, ideally 535–570°F to approximate a wood-fired oven.

19. Load the loaf.

20. After 20 minutes, reduce the oven to 400°F.

21. Continue baking for 70–90 minutes, until the crust is thick and deeply browned.

22. Turn off the oven.

23. Leave the bread inside with the door slightly open for 10 minutes.

24. Cool completely on a rack.

Service

Serve only after completely cooling.

Chef's note

The large loaf size and long bake create the robust crust that protects the crumb and extends keeping quality.

title: Pitta Calabrese
instructions:
Pitta Calabrese

Calabrian ring-shaped bread, soft inside and deeply golden outside.

Yield: 1 large pitta

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp type 0 or all-purpose flour
1 1/4 cups warm water
about 2 tsp fresh yeast
1 2/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in the warm water.

2. Put the flour in a large bowl.

3. Gradually add the yeast water.

4. Knead until the dough begins to become smooth.

5. Add the salt.

6. Add the olive oil.

7. Knead for 8–10 minutes, until uniform and elastic.

8. Cover.

9. Let rise until doubled, about 1 1/2–2 hours.

10. Dust a baking sheet with the flour.

11. Turn the dough onto the work surface.

12. Shape into a ball.

13. Make a hole in the center.

14. Gently widen into a broad flattened ring.

15. Transfer to the baking sheet.

16. Cover.

17. Rest for 30 minutes.

18. Preheat a conventional oven to 425°F.

19. Bake for 20–25 minutes, until puffed and deeply golden.

20. Cool slightly on a rack.

Service

Serve warm or use as a bread for filling.

Chef's note

Make the center opening generous before baking because it narrows as the dough expands.

title: Sweet Pitta ’Mpigliata
instructions:
Sweet Pitta ’Mpigliata

Calabrian rolled pastry with walnuts, raisins, sugar, and warm spices.

Yield: 10–12 servings

Ingredients

For the dough
4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
1 cup plus 1 tbsp warm water
about 1 tbsp fresh yeast
3 1/2 tbsp lard
1/4 cup granulated sugar
1/3 tsp fine salt

For the filling
about 1 2/3 cups chopped walnuts
1 cup raisins
1/2 cup granulated sugar
1 tsp ground cinnamon
1/2 tsp ground cloves
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

Preparation

1. Soak the raisins in warm water for 15 minutes.

2. Drain and dry.

3. Dissolve the yeast in the warm water.

4. Put the flour in a large bowl.

5. Gradually add the yeast water.

6. Add the lard, sugar, and salt.

7. Knead for 10 minutes, until smooth and uniform.

8. Cover.

9. Let rise until doubled, about 1 1/2–2 hours.

10. Mix the walnuts, raisins, sugar, cinnamon, and cloves.

11. Roll the dough into a large thin rectangle.

12. Brush with 2 tablespoons olive oil.

13. Spread the filling evenly.

14. Roll from a long side.

15. Cut into pieces about 1 1/2–2 inches thick.

16. Grease a 9 1/2-inch cake pan with the remaining olive oil.

17. Arrange the pieces upright and close together in the pan.

18. Cover.

19. Proof for another 30–45 minutes.

20. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

21. Bake for 35–40 minutes, until evenly golden.

22. Cool completely before unmolding.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Arrange the spirals close together without compressing them so they can expand and remain visible after baking.

title: Pane di Cutro
instructions:
Pane di Cutro

Calabrian naturally leavened bread made with durum semolina and soft-wheat flour.

Yield: 2 medium loaves

Ingredients

3 1/2 cups finely milled durum semolina
3 1/3 cups type 0 or all-purpose flour
about 1 1/2 cups active natural starter

1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

2. Mix the semolina and soft-wheat flour.

3. Tear the starter into pieces.

4. Add it to the flours.

5. Add about 2 1/3 cups water.

6. Knead for 12–15 minutes.

7. Dissolve the salt in the remaining scant 1/2 cup water.

8. Gradually work in the salted water.

9. Continue kneading until firm, uniform, and elastic.

10. Cover.

11. Let rise naturally for 4–6 hours.

12. Turn onto a lightly floured work surface.

13. Divide in half.

14. Shape into rounds or elongated loaves.

15. Dust lightly with flour or semolina.

16. Cover.

17. Proof for about 1 hour.

18. Preheat the oven with a baking stone or heavy sheet to 465°F.

19. Score the loaves.

20. Load into the oven.

21. Bake for 20 minutes at 465°F.

22. Reduce the oven to 375°F.

23. Continue baking for 50–60 minutes, until the crust is thick and crisp.

24. Cool completely on a rack.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

The combination of semolina and soft-wheat flour creates a porous but resilient crumb and the bread’s characteristic golden color.
